question: Why does a production React application often adopt Next.js instead of staying a plain client-only Vite SPA?
options: Plain React cannot render JSX without a Next.js server running in Node.js
Next.js adds server rendering, file-system routing, automatic route code splitting, caching, and backend integration on top of React
Vite does not support TypeScript or CSS modules in React components
React hooks like useState only work inside Next.js applications
explanation: React is a UI library focused on rendering components. Next.js provides the surrounding full-stack framework infrastructure: file-system routing, server rendering, code splitting, caching, and asset optimization.

question: Which file in the app/ directory is required at the root and must render the <html> and <body> tags?
options: app/page.tsx
next.config.ts
app/layout.tsx
public/index.html
explanation: The root app/layout.tsx file wraps every route in the App Router and must define the top-level <html> and <body> elements.

question: In the App Router, what happens if you create app/dashboard/ChartHelper.tsx without creating a page.tsx in that folder?
options: ChartHelper.tsx is safely colocated and is not exposed as a public URL route
Next.js throws a build error because every file inside app/ must export a route
Users can visit /dashboard/ChartHelper in the browser to render that component
Next.js automatically moves ChartHelper.tsx into the public/ folder
explanation: In the App Router, only folders containing a page.tsx (or route.ts) become publicly addressable routes. Other files inside app/ are safely colocated without becoming URLs.

question: Which CLI command compiles your Next.js application into optimized production bundles before starting the server?
options: next dev
next start
next lint
next build
explanation: next build compiles and optimizes server and client bundles for production. After building, next start launches the production server, whereas next dev runs the local development server with Turbopack.

question: How does the App Router treat a newly created component file inside app/ that has no directives at the top?
options: It runs exclusively in the browser and includes all imports in the client JavaScript bundle
It executes as a React Server Component by default, keeping its code off the client bundle
It compiles into a legacy Pages Router getServerSideProps function
It refuses to render unless you add 'use server' on line 1
explanation: Every component in the App Router is a React Server Component by default. You only add 'use client' to files that require browser interactivity like state, effects, or DOM event handlers.
